newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul probes second Daewoo official in arms scam.
newsitem.headline: Seoul probes second Daewoo official in arms scam.

text.p: State prosecutors summoned a second executive of South Korea's Daewoo Group on Wednesday in connection with an arms scandal involving a former defence minister, prosecution officials said.

The prosecutors, who grilled Daewoo Group Chairman Yoon Young-suk on Tuesday, summoned him again on Wednesday along with Chung Ho-shin, vice president of Daewoo Heavy Industries Ltd, a member firm of the group, they said.
"Mr Yoon and Mr Chung are being interrogated in the prosecution building," one official said, declining to give any other details.

President Kim Young-sam ordered an investigation into the scandal last week after an opposition party alleged Daewoo Heavy paid bribes of 300 million won ($362,000) to an arms dealer last year to arrange a government purchase of military helicopters.

The dealer paid half the money to former defence minister Lee Yang-ho, who was sacked last week by Kim, according to the allegations made in parliament by the main opposition National Congress for New Politics.
Lee Yang-ho has denied the accusations, according to local media reports.
Yoon, who is also chief executive officer of Daewoo Heavy, a leading government arms contractor, told reporters that his company was deceived by the arms dealer but gave no details.
A Daewoo Group spokesman Kim Yoon-shik said Daewoo Heavy had paid money to arms dealer Kwon Pyong-ho, but not as a bribe.
"The amount did not exceed 300 million won. But it was a commission and not bribery. We have been framed by this fake. That's all we can say at the moment," Kim said on Tuesday.

The affair has embarrassed the president, who has staked his reputation on rooting out corruption in high places in a campaign that has led to the trial and conviction of former presidents Roh Tae-woo and Chun Doo Hwan.
Daewoo Group founder Kim Woo-choong is currently appealing a two-year jail sentence imposed for bribing Roh. He was one of nine businessmen convicted on similar charges.

Former president Chun was sentenced to death and Roh to 22-1/2 years in jail after being convicted in August on charges of corruption, mutiny and treason. Both men are currently appealing their convictions.
